# A selected one-group critical star cover admits an actual joint escape

Fix d>=2. Let K be a centered full-dimensional d-simplex, V=|K|,
B=K-K, U=|B|. The actual convex hull with integer fibers

    K at z=-1,    B at z=0,    -K at z=1

has mixed mass M=2V+U and actual maximum depth D=M/2. Retain just
one proper concurrent vertex-parallel star group, as specified below.
Then this body and selected cover are NOT a local volume maximum
when the group parameters and the free endpoint simplex may vary.

If the group's endpoint thresholds are nonuniform, its caps can stay
fixed while an endpoint motion increases volume and strictly decreases
all their global masses. At the canonical threshold, there is an
explicit analytic joint path with a positive cubic volume gain and a
strict cubic decrease of every selected cap. These conclusions hold
in every joint neighborhood of the original body and cap parameters.

Only the selected cover's budgets are retained. The theorem does not
preserve the budgets of all the discarded redundant star groups.
The word selected does not claim minimum cardinality among every
possible covering family.

## 1. The actual critical source and its selected group

Write the barycentric coordinates of K as

    lambda_i(x)=l_i(x)+1/m,    m=d+1,    sum_i l_i=0,

where each l_i is linear. Choose

    0<a_i<1,    sum_i a_i=1,

and retain the m ambient closed caps

    H_i(a)={l_i(x)+(a_i-1/m)z>=0}.                    (1)

Their margins sum to zero, so the group covers the entire
R x R^d, for every such a. Their boundaries pass through (0,0).
On K at z=-1 they are lambda_i>=a_i. On -K at z=1,
reflection converts them to lambda_i<=a_i on K. Consequently
the two endpoint masses sum to V, and the middle cap mass is U/2.
All selected caps therefore have exactly the same mass

    mu(H_i(a))=D=V+U/2,                              (2)

independently of a.

The source is invariant under (z,x)->(-z,-x). Every nonvertical
through-origin cap has half of its mass, since its boundary is null
in each full-dimensional fiber. A vertical containing cap has at least
half the source mass as well. This proves depth at (0,0) at least D.
Two opposite nonvertical through-origin caps bound every candidate's
depth above by D. Thus D is the actual maximum, including all
vertical and closed-boundary cases.

The selected group is inclusion-minimal on this source: at the i-th
vertex of the left endpoint, only H_i(a) is satisfied, and this
exclusivity persists in a positive-volume neighborhood inside that
endpoint. This does not assert that the group's size is the minimum
over all unrestricted ambient covers.

## 2. Exact global budget transfer and physical compatibility

Represent a nearby labeled endpoint simplex K(W) by a barycentric
vertex matrix W, with column sums one and W near I. Keep B and -K
fixed. If F_i(W,a) denotes the ordinary volume of K(W) in
lambda_i>=a_i, then for EVERY proper a, including a that varies
along a path, the exact global identity is

    mu_W(H_i(a))=D+F_i(W,a)-F_i(I,a).                (3)

The unchanged reflected endpoint contributes V-F_i(I,a), and the
unchanged symmetric middle contributes U/2. There is no removal
or replacement of a source fiber in (3).

For clarity, the available midpoint slack has a simple quantitative
barycentric certificate. In the continuous direction space sum y_i=0,

    K-K={y: sum_i (y_i)_+ <=1}.

Indeed a difference of two simplex probability vectors has positive
coordinate sum at most one, and conversely its positive and negative
parts can be completed by a common nonnegative vector to such
probability vectors. If every column of W-I has l1 norm less than 2,
then for every pair of indices j,k,

    sum_i ((W e_j-e_k)/2)_+
            <=1/2+||W e_j-e_j||_1/4 <1.            (4)

This uses that each column difference has coordinate sum zero.
Every vertex pair of (K(W)+(-K))/2 is therefore strictly inside B.
Their convex hull is compactly contained there. Hence the actual
convex hull over bases -1,0,1 has exactly K(W), B, -K as its
integer fibers. Endpoints are exposed in the base, so they are exact
without an additional interpolation condition.

For sufficiently small W-I the determinant is positive and every
cap keeps its one-positive-vertex cut pattern. Its exact formula is

    F_i(W,a)/V
       =det W (W_ii-a_i)^d/product_(j!=i)(W_ii-W_ij).           (5)

For example, a bound ||W-I||_1<1/2 ensures invertibility and (4);
entrywise distance less than half min_i{a_i,1-a_i} ensures the
strict cap pattern. The remaining strict gain signs below follow
from the explicit derivatives of (5).

## 3. A constructive escape at any nonuniform proper threshold

We reproduce the needed velocity construction from the independently
audited simplex-fixed-cap-first-order-rigidity-and-explicit-descent.md.
It uses only physical endpoint vertex motions while the group a
stays fixed.

Put

    h_i=d(1-a_i)^(d-1),    H=sum_i 1/h_i,
    J_ij=a_j+(a_i-1)/d,    i!=j.

For a nonuniform a with sum a_i=1, some J_ij is nonzero. Select
one, let sigma=sign J_ij, and let E have entries E_ij=sigma,
E_jj=-sigma and all other entries zero. Write f_i(E) for the
normalized first derivative F_i'(I,a)[E]/V.

For a desired normalized cap derivative vector f, set z_i=f_i/h_i,
Z=sum_i z_i, and define

    S_a(f)_ii=z_i,
    S_a(f)_ij=z_i-Z/d             for i!=j.

It has zero column sums, normalized cap derivatives exactly f,
and trace sum_i f_i/h_i. Let J=|J_ij| and

    epsilon=J/(2H),
    A(a)=E-S_a(f(E))+S_a(-epsilon*1).               (6)

Direct differentiation of (5) gives

    tr A(a)=J/2>0,
    F_i'(I,a)[A(a)]/V=-epsilon<0   for every i.      (7)

Thus W(t)=I+t A(a), with a fixed, is an actual admissible endpoint
path for all sufficiently small positive t, and

    M(t)=M+V(J/2)t+O(t^2),
    mu_t(H_i(a))=D-V epsilon t+O(t^2).              (8)

Equations (3)-(5) justify every global cap budget and exact fiber
identity in this statement. The finitely many remainders allow one
common positive time interval. The group still covers the entire
ambient space, so (8) in particular bounds the actual maximum
depth strictly below D on this perturbed three-fiber source.

## 4. The canonical group: an explicit analytic cubic escape

Suppose a(0)=m^(-1)*1. The single fixed canonical group need not
admit the first-order endpoint motion (7). We therefore move its
base-normal coefficients as well, preserving the common contact
and the full-space cover:

    a(t)=m^(-1)*1+t(e_1-e_0),    t>=0.              (9)

For 0<t<1/m all its thresholds are proper. Use the fixed elementary
pair (i,j)=(0,1) in (6), with positive sign. Its coefficient is

    J_01(a(t))=(d-1)t/d>0.

The construction A(a(t)) is analytic at t=0 when defined by this
fixed pair and sign: all h_i remain positive, S_a is analytic,
and epsilon vanishes linearly. Now set

    W(t)=I+t^2 A(a(t)).                              (10)

This is a single analytic joint path through the original body and
the canonical group. Its cap motions have size O(t) and its
physical endpoint motion has size O(t^2), so it enters every
prescribed joint neighborhood as t tends to zero.

By (7), tr A(a(t))=(d-1)t/(2d). At the canonical threshold,
h_i=m Gamma_d and H(0)=1/Gamma_d, where Gamma_d=(d/m)^d.
Expanding the exact formulas (3) and (5) consequently gives

    M(t)=M+V(d-1)t^3/(2d)+O(t^4),

    mu_t(H_i(a(t)))
         =D-Gamma_d V(d-1)t^3/(2d)+O(t^4)           (11)

for every selected cap. The leading coefficients have strict signs.
All selected budgets are therefore strictly improved for every
sufficiently small positive t. This is stronger than a two-step
argument that first moves the cap parameters at constant mass (2)
and then applies (8).

The restriction d>=2 matters: the positive coefficient in (9)
vanishes in dimension one. No conclusion for that case is inferred
from this construction.

## 5. Every joint neighborhood contains a strict feasible improvement

For nonuniform a this follows from (8) with fixed caps. For canonical
a it follows from the analytic path (9)-(11), which converges in both
the finite vertex coordinates and the ambient cap coefficients.
Thus the initial star is not a local volume maximum in the enlarged
problem with just this one selected group's original budgets D.

This does not contradict a local maximum under all the fixed caps of
the redundant variance example. The selected constraints define a
different feasible set. No statement that the discarded budgets
remain feasible is made.

## 6. Binary isolated extensions preserve all retained budgets

The same escape works in the binary embedding from
actual-critical-caps-can-have-stationary-threshold-variance.md.
For n>=2, write the base as (z,w), with w in R^(n-1).
At w=0 retain the star at z=-1,0,1. At each other binary w=v,
place a centered simplex of volume D/Gamma_d at each of z=0,1.
Take the actual convex hull.

Conditioning on a binary w in a convex combination forces every
source point in that combination to have that same w. Consequently
the exact integer support is the three star bases and the two
regular bases at each v!=0, with no other integer fibers. In
particular (4) is the only new compatibility check for the star
endpoint motion.

Retain only the one star group, isolated by a finite tilt

    l_i(x)+(a_i-1/m)z-L sum_k w_k>=0.

Choose L with a strict exclusion margin on every regular fiber,
uniformly for a in a small compact neighborhood of its initial
value. This is possible because there are finitely many compact
regular fibers and their sums of binary coordinates are at least
one. These star caps have exactly the original star masses and
cover the star component.
If an initial isolating L is already fixed with strict margins,
continuity provides such a neighborhood for that same L; no change
of the isolation coefficient is necessary for the local escape.

For each regular base retain its isolated canonical group, using
the exposing functional and finite isolation tilt in the cited
construction. All other fibers, including the moving star endpoint,
are strictly excluded. Hence these regular cap masses stay EXACTLY
D throughout a sufficiently small star endpoint path. Their own
fibers do not change. The selected star caps satisfy (8) or (11)
and strictly decrease; every retained original budget is preserved.

Coverage of every actual integer fiber persists: the selected star
group covers the entire star fiber spaces, and each regular group
covers its entire own fiber space. The selected family is
inclusion-minimal on the displayed source, since each canonical or
proper vertex cap has an own-fiber vertex neighborhood strictly
excluded by all the other retained caps. Its number of groups is
1+(2^n-2)=2^n-1; no minimum possible group count is asserted.

For n>=2, an unchanged regular simplex centroid has actual depth at
least D, from its own fiber alone. The retained cover has every cap
mass at most D, giving the matching upper bound on every candidate.
Thus the actual absolute maximum stays exactly D in this binary
extension, while total mixed mass strictly increases. In the lone
three-fiber star, every retained cap decreases and the actual
absolute maximum also strictly decreases.

This is an actual local escape for the selected cover, not a proof
that an arbitrary critical cover admits such a selection, and not
a general extremizer classification.

The standard-library verifier
../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_selected_one_group_critical_star_escape.py passes 22 exact
first-order, formal cubic-series and actual compatible-path checks
in dimensions 2 through 8, together with 168 actual planar isolated
cap-budget checks for binary embeddings in ranks 2 through 5.
At the planar canonical-path time t=1/1000, the exact absolute
volume gain is 15984000001/128000000000000000000>0. The cubic
series proof above supplies the all-dimensional local conclusion.
